title: Lesson counts are forecasts to test
statement: Treat a course's lesson counts as forecasts to test on a timed pilot unit, and when the material needs more time, re-plan the calendar rather than cut content or teaching.
example: One plan forecast 130 teaching sessions and left the rest of the framework's suggested periods for assessment, review and remediation.
detail: An AP history course plan forecast 130 teaching sessions against the framework's 140 suggested class periods, reserving the difference for assessments, cumulative review, remediation and final exam practice, and made its first unit the pacing pilot. Its rule is that the counts are assumptions to test: measured time on that unit triggers a whole-course reforecast, and the plan never keeps a neat count by removing difficult content, shortening source work or treating assessment as instruction. If the estimate grows, the calendar changes or only genuinely co-dependent topics are combined.
against: Never exercised: the status file reports "130 of 130 declared teaching sessions" (grade3-reading/_archive/2026-08-13-consolidation/apush-corpus-hardening-20260731-tip.tar.gz:apush/docs/FULL-COURSE-AUTHORING-STATUS.md, line 9), the forecast count unchanged, and "Target-runtime import, rendering, and scoring verification | Not run" (line 50), so no timed pilot tested the forecast.

evidence.quote: The proposed lesson counts are assumptions to test. If Unit 1 requires more time for source access, writing, or correction, the whole-course forecast changes. The plan does not preserve a neat count by removing difficult content, shortening source work, or treating assessment as instruction.

If the estimate grows, adjust the calendar or combine only genuinely co-dependent topics. Never delete a KC, replace teaching with an item set, or compress a source-analysis handoff into an answer reveal.

Unit 1 is the pacing pilot and includes its checkpoint inside the eight-period slice. Its measured authoring and eventual student-runtime evidence trigger a whole-course reforecast; scope is not silently deleted to preserve the estimate.

Its proposed 130 teaching sessions are an authoring forecast, not a fixed school calendar. The official framework suggests 140 class periods; the difference is reserved for assessments, cumulative review, remediation, and final exam practice.
